system: You are the independent Pattern inducer for an evidence-grounded resolution graph. Use only the supplied training Workflows and Actions. A Pattern is a plain-language cross-project decision policy, not a category label, repository recipe, or claim that different Actions are interchangeable. Preserve distinct Action contracts. Express the reusable structure as role-level action_template entries and bind each supporting Workflow to the exact Action ids that realize those roles. State when to use the Pattern, anti-goals, exclusions, decision branches, ordering, and validation. Use candidate_pending_holdout only when at least two repositories support every required role; it still requires a separate untouched holdout repair. Never invent holdout facts, solution refs, tests, evidence ids, Action ids, or Workflow ids. Return JSON only.

instructions: Give the Pattern a short title a software engineer can understand without knowing AREX.
Describe observable applicability signals, not product names or issue numbers.
Do not merge Actions. Use workflow_realizations to map generic roles to existing ids.
A required role must be independently realized in at least two repositories.
Keep repository-specific branches conditional rather than universally mandatory.
The validation ladder must distinguish focused contract checks, integration checks, and regressions.
If the evidence supports only fragments rather than one coherent policy, return defer.

pattern_candidate.intent: Resolve structured tool contract integrity through a contract-first, evidence-validated change chain.
pattern_candidate.extraction_method: structural-action-fingerprint-v1; semantic judge required before promotion

workflows.name: harden_structured_tool_completion_proofs
workflows.title: Harden structured tool-call completion proofs
workflows.description: A fail-closed resolution chain for completion metadata that crosses session history, asynchronous exec/wait wrappers, retries, compaction, and bounded prompt serialization.
workflows.goal: Emit a positive structured completion claim only when the host retains an unambiguous, lossless chain from a fresh invocation through its nested calls and matching output, while preserving valid claims for unrelated cells.
when_to_use: A host records nested tool activity and exposes a structured completeness marker to a later model request or downstream consumer.
Invocation or runtime identifiers can be reused across retries, compaction, resume, fork, or asynchronous wait operations.
Recorded evidence is subject to per-call or aggregate serialization budgets.
Recording policy can change during a long-lived session.
anti_goals: Do not change tool execution availability, dispatch gates, or nested-tool behavior merely to change recording policy.
Do not infer completeness from a successful wrapper callback, terminal wait, or retained marker when association or inventory evidence is missing.
Do not discard trustworthy metadata for unrelated cells solely because one cell exceeded a budget.
Do not use unbounded sets or unbounded hashing to prove identifier freshness.
not_applicable_when: The metadata is informational only and no consumer interprets it as a complete inventory or proof.
Invocation identifiers and output associations are guaranteed unique and immutable by a stronger external protocol, with no retries, resume, fork, compaction, or truncation boundary.
No host-side execution evidence can be inspected; in that case a positive completion contract cannot be established.
inputs: Initial session history, including compacted replacement history when available
Live tool input and output items with call identifiers and tool type information
Runtime cell identifiers and originating wrapper identifiers
Recorded nested-call inventory and retained retry state
Per-argument, per-output, and aggregate metadata budgets
Current and incoming runtime recording feature state
workflows.entry_state: The system can record nested calls, but identifier freshness, wrapper association, retry integrity, budget truncation, or runtime enablement may allow an unsupported completeness marker.
workflows.exit_state: Every positive completion marker is backed by fresh identifiers, a unique matching input/output association, and an intact recorded inventory within the serialized prompt; ambiguous or damaged cells are incomplete, unrelated intact cells remain complete, and recording policy changes do not alter execution behavior.

steps.condition: Always required when identifiers can cross history or recorder-lifetime boundaries.
steps.validation: Known historical and repeated identifiers return non-fresh; failed indexing prevents cell start from becoming completion-eligible.

steps.condition: Apply when attaching recorded evidence to outputs or replaying retained evidence after retry or compaction.
steps.validation: Each certified output has exactly one preceding type-correct exec or wait input, matching origin/runtime handle, no direct-call collision, and an intact retained inventory.

steps.condition: Apply before sending or storing metadata whenever argument or aggregate limits can truncate recorded evidence.
steps.validation: Damaged cells lose completion across their outputs, their omission marker remains local, and unrelated intact cells retain completion under the global budget.

steps.condition: Apply when recorder enablement is controlled by runtime rollout or configuration refresh.
steps.validation: Runtime enablement changes recorder allocation without changing execution features; late enablement cannot certify unobserved history; legacy reload keeps the live recorder.

validation_ladder: Unit-test bounded identifier tracking, namespace separation, saturation, historical indexing limits, and repeated-ID rejection.
Test recorder state transitions for lossless completion, duplicate nested IDs, wrapper mismatches, direct-call collisions, forked or resumed waits, retries, and compaction.
Test protocol serialization budgets to confirm optional metadata is shed before core evidence and completion is revoked only for damaged cells.
Run end-to-end asynchronous tool scenarios for runtime enablement, configuration refresh, resumed handle reuse, compaction, and unrelated-output truncation.
stop_conditions: Stop and withhold completeness if initial-history identifiers cannot be indexed within bounds and freshness is required.
Stop and invalidate the affected cell if an origin, runtime handle, or nested call ID is reused or collides.
Stop and invalidate retained completion if an output is duplicated, lacks one matching preceding input, changes inventory, or no longer matches its exec/wait wrapper.
Stop and clear completion for the affected cell when truncation or omission prevents retention of its full call inventory.
Stop extraction-level validation short of claiming a green build because the evidence bundle contains test sources but no executed status-check or test-command result.
unresolved_or_deferred: The GitHub bundle lacks PR discussion, reviews, and status-check results.
No test command was executed as part of this extraction, so repository-wide runtime validation remains unconfirmed.
The bounded bitmap intentionally permits false-positive collisions that withhold completion; its production collision rate is not established by this episode.

workflows.name: bound-semantic-tool-call-stagnation
workflows.title: Add a precise circuit breaker for argument-varying tool stagnation
workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for detecting repeated tool requests that differ textually but share one non-progressing semantic operation, while preserving productive variants and propagating a structured halt contract.
workflows.goal: Halt a bounded run of semantically equivalent, non-progressing tool requests even when their raw arguments vary, without stopping productive or targeted operations.
when_to_use: A tool loop evades exact request equality because the model rewrites arguments while repeating the same observable read-only operation.
The repeated operation has a narrow semantic class with evidence-backed exclusions precise enough for an always-on or high-confidence guard.
The runtime already has a termination path capable of discarding queued calls and emitting a structured reason.
anti_goals: Do not classify all repeated uses of one tool name as equivalent.
Do not stop write-bearing, mixed-purpose, targeted-review, or otherwise progress-bearing operations merely because they contain an inspection segment.
Do not place the new precise guard behind a broad heuristic-skip setting when the intended contract is always-on, though an explicit session-level disable may remain honored.
Do not alter unrelated content, thought, read-file, alternating-call, or hard-cap detectors.
not_applicable_when: No stable semantic equivalence class can be derived from the structured request or command payload.
The suspected loop includes productive state changes or target-specific narrowing that constitutes progress.
Only issue-title or similarity evidence exists without an implementation diff and validation oracle.
The consumer has no safe halt path for cancelling queued operations and reporting the reason.
inputs: Representative looping request variants
Counterexamples that must count as progress
Structured tool name and argument payload
Consecutive-streak threshold
Retry, prompt-reset, and session-disable lifecycle semantics
Typed loop-event, telemetry, and user-message contracts
workflows.entry_state: Exact request equality does not catch a repeated semantic operation because each consecutive request varies its arguments, so the run can continue until a distant generic cap or external failure.
workflows.exit_state: Only the proven non-progressing request class shares a semantic key; its uninterrupted streak halts at the configured bound, progress and replay boundaries reset it, excluded operations continue, and all consumers receive one structured halt reason.

steps.condition: Use only after positive loop variants and productive counterexamples establish a narrow semantic boundary.
steps.validation: Positive overview-inspection variants share one key, while write-bearing, mixed, non-repository, and path-specific cases do not.

steps.condition: Apply when consecutive requests receive the admitted semantic key and detection is not explicitly disabled for the session.
steps.validation: The threshold request fires; threshold-minus-one does not; nonmatching requests, retries, and prompt resets restart counting.

steps.condition: Apply whenever the new circuit breaker reports detection.
steps.validation: The production stream clears pending calls, emits the dedicated reason, terminates, logs telemetry, and provides a matching user-facing explanation.

validation_ladder: Classifier unit boundary: admit distinct overview-style read-only variants and reject productive, mixed-purpose, unrelated, and targeted operations.
State-machine boundary: verify threshold-minus-one, exact threshold, interruption reset, retry reset, prompt reset, and explicit session disable.
Integration boundary: confirm the guard executes before configuration-gated heuristics and clears queued requests on detection.
Contract boundary: confirm one dedicated reason is consistent across detector state, emitted stream event, telemetry, and user-facing text.
Repository validation: run the focused loop-detection test file in a clean checkout with the repository's declared runtime and package manager.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if semantic equivalence cannot be expressed narrowly enough to avoid known productive cases.
Stop if the detector cannot reset on observable progress or replay boundaries.
Stop if a firing cannot safely cancel pending requests and terminate the current run.
Do not claim runtime validation until the focused tests execute successfully in a usable checkout.
unresolved_or_deferred: The issue and PR bodies, comments, reviews, timeline, and status checks are unavailable in the evidence bundle.
The focused regression suite was inspected but not executed because this workspace exposes a deleted working tree and lacks the runtime executable.
No cross-repository resolution pattern is proposed from this single workflow.

workflows.name: repair-leaking-truncated-structured-call-fragments
workflows.title: Repair leaked truncated tool-call fragments while preserving ordinary prose
workflows.description: A bounded workflow for a sanitizer that already removes malformed structured calls but misses a newly observed serialization prefix. It narrows the grammar change to the smallest evidenced prefix class and validates both removal and non-removal behavior across content consumers.
workflows.goal: Remove unrecoverable name-prefixed structured-call fragments from assistant content at every relevant sanitization boundary without deleting natural-language mentions or later unrelated prose.
when_to_use: A structured-output sanitizer already handles line-leading argument tags, but raw markup leaks when the first tag is directly attached to a bare identifier-like call name.
The malformed fragment is unrecoverable and should be removed rather than parsed or executed.
More than one consumer boundary is expected to enforce the same stripping contract.
anti_goals: Do not interpret, reconstruct, or execute the truncated call.
Do not accept arbitrary prose before an argument tag as a fragment prefix.
Do not remove unrelated preceding or subsequent visible prose.
Do not redesign complete structured-call parsing or unrelated reasoning-tag handling.
not_applicable_when: The input is a complete, valid structured call that should be parsed through the normal tool-call path.
The suspected prefix contains spaces or sentence text and cannot be distinguished from an inline prose example by the evidenced identifier-only rule.
The affected consumer does not use the shared line-oriented stripping contract.
There is no reproducible malformed input and preservation oracle.
inputs: A captured malformed assistant-content sample
The sanitizer's existing line-boundary grammar
The set of display and storage sanitizer consumers
Positive removal expectations and negative prose-preservation examples
workflows.entry_state: Raw argument markup from a truncated structured call can survive because a bare call name appears immediately before the first argument tag, while existing behavior already protects ordinary inline prose.
workflows.exit_state: Identifier-only name-prefixed fragments are removed by all tested sanitizer consumers, preceding visible text is retained, and spaced inline prose plus unrelated trailing prose remain protected.

steps.condition: The failing sample has a line-boundary identifier-like prefix directly glued to an arg_key or arg_value tag.
steps.validation: The matcher admits the observed complete and value-truncated prefixed shapes, while its prefix character class cannot span spaces into ordinary prose.

steps.condition: Display and storage paths are both contractually expected to strip tool-call markup.
steps.validation: Parameterized cases produce only the visible prefix for both sanitizer variants, and prose-preservation cases remain unchanged.

validation_ladder: Confirm the parent matcher excludes the captured name-prefixed shape.
Check the revised grammar admits only the evidenced identifier-like attached prefix.
Verify complete and value-truncated name-prefixed fragments are removed while their preceding visible lines remain.
Run the same cases against display and storage sanitizers.
Verify inline prose containing argument tags and subsequent unrelated prose survive.
stop_conditions: Stop if the prefix requires whitespace or arbitrary sentence text; the evidenced bounded grammar no longer distinguishes it safely from prose.
Stop if the fragment is recoverable through the normal complete-call parser rather than an unrecoverable sanitization case.
Stop if any preservation oracle shows deletion of ordinary prose or unrelated trailing content.
Stop before claiming runtime test success when the test runner is unavailable.
unresolved_or_deferred: The checkout environment does not provide the pytest executable, so the regression suite could not be executed during extraction.
The GitHub bundle contains no PR body, review discussion, or status-check results; no CI outcome is claimed.

workflows.name: restore-versioned-tool-call-correlation
workflows.title: Restore tool-call correlation at a versioned protocol boundary
workflows.description: Repair structured history conversion when a newer protocol generation requires explicit identifiers on both tool calls and their responses, without changing older-version wire behavior.
workflows.goal: Ensure every tool call and corresponding tool result retain a matching explicit identifier when the target protocol version requires correlation IDs.
when_to_use: A conversation adapter receives internally correlated tool calls and results but emits structured history without their identifiers.
The requirement begins at an identifiable model or protocol version boundary.
One shared capability predicate already controls both call-side and response-side ID serialization.
anti_goals: Do not add IDs unconditionally to older protocol versions whose established wire representation omits them.
Do not create separate provider-specific conversion paths when both adapters consume the shared converter.
Do not alter thought-signature handling, tool payloads, or result content while repairing identifier correlation.
not_applicable_when: The internal history lacks stable identifiers linking tool results to tool calls.
Only one side of the external protocol accepts an identifier and paired call-response equality is not its contract.
The affected adapters do not share the capability predicate or serialization boundary.
inputs: Target model or protocol identifier
Version parser or equivalent capability metadata
Conversation history with tool calls and matching tool results
Shared message-conversion entry point
Representative older and newer version cases
workflows.entry_state: A newer protocol generation is routed through a shared converter, but the capability predicate excludes it, so call and response IDs are dropped during replay.
workflows.exit_state: The required protocol generation emits matching IDs on every serialized function call and function response through each shared adapter, while the tested older generation continues omitting IDs.

steps.condition: The ID requirement can be expressed as a stable family or major-version capability boundary.
steps.validation: Direct boundary cases return the expected capability result without regressing previously supported families.

steps.condition: Both function-call and function-response serialization consult the shared capability decision.
steps.validation: A multi-call history produces equal ordered IDs on call and response parts for every consuming adapter, and produces no IDs for the excluded older version.

validation_ladder: Unit-check the capability predicate immediately below and above the version boundary.
Serialize at least two tool calls and matching results to detect missing, duplicated, or reordered correlation IDs.
Assert equality of call-side and response-side identifier sequences.
Run the same history through every adapter that consumes the shared converter.
Assert an older protocol version preserves its prior omission behavior.
Retain unrelated structured-message assertions, including thought-signature behavior.
stop_conditions: Stop if the protocol's explicit-ID requirement cannot be established from implementation or tests.
Stop if internal tool results cannot be mapped to their originating calls.
Stop if enabling the capability changes older-version serialization.
Stop if only call IDs or only response IDs survive the conversion.
unresolved_or_deferred: The GitHub bundle contains no PR body, issue discussion, review rationale, or status-check results.
No independent test execution result was supplied; validation is grounded in the committed test oracle.

actions.intent: Ensure a detector firing produces an actionable, consistently typed halt rather than allowing queued work to continue or reporting an ambiguous failure.
actions.pre_state: The always-on detector has returned true and recorded the semantic stagnation loop type while pending tool requests may exist.
actions.post_state: Pending requests are discarded, a typed loop event is emitted, the turn terminates through the existing cleanup path, telemetry can distinguish the reason, and headless output explains the halt and configuration behavior.
actions.validation: Inspect the production call site and reporting mappings to confirm the same loop type drives cleanup, stream output, telemetry, and the human-readable message.
actions.description: Carry the newly detected reason through telemetry, stream termination, pending-call cleanup, and user-facing reporting so consumers observe a consistent contract.

actions.intent: Prevent raw structured-call argument markup from reaching visible or stored assistant text when a truncated serialization begins with a bare tool name.
actions.module_role: Malformed structured-output sanitizer shared by assistant-content consumers
actions.pre_state: A line contains a truncated argument-tag serialization whose first tag is glued to a bare identifier-like call name, and the sanitizer only recognizes tags that directly begin the line.
actions.post_state: The name-prefixed fragment is classified as unrecoverable structured output and removed, while prefixes containing prose-separating spaces remain outside this new match shape.
actions.validation: Apply the sanitizer to complete and cut name-prefixed fragments and verify that only the preceding visible text remains; also verify that spaced inline prose examples survive.
actions.description: Extend a line-oriented malformed-call detector to admit only an identifier-like prefix attached directly to an argument tag, preserving its existing line boundary and prose-safety constraints.

actions.intent: Establish a regression oracle showing that every relevant assistant-content boundary removes the newly recognized malformed fragments without broadening deletion into ordinary prose.
actions.pre_state: Multiple content sanitizers are expected to provide equivalent tool-call tag coverage, but the name-prefixed truncated-fragment shape lacks an explicit shared regression case.
actions.post_state: Both display and storage sanitizer variants are checked against complete and cut name-prefixed fragments, and preservation tests constrain false-positive removal.
actions.validation: Run the parameterized fragment test for both sanitizer variants and the adjacent prose-preservation tests; the expected outputs retain visible prefixes and remove malformed markup.
actions.description: Encode the malformed inputs and preservation expectations once, then exercise both consumer-facing sanitizers to prevent their structured-output contracts from diverging.

actions.intent: Withhold completeness when wrappers, outputs, retries, or resumed runtime handles are ambiguous or inconsistent.
actions.pre_state: Recorded calls may be attached to duplicated outputs, mismatched wrappers, reused origins, colliding direct calls, resumed waits, or retry history whose association evidence has changed.
actions.post_state: Only a unique, ordered, type-correct association can retain completeness, and once the associated inventory or mapping is invalidated all retained outputs for that runtime cell remain incomplete.
actions.validation: Recorder regressions cover mismatched wrappers, reused origins, duplicate IDs, forked waits, and retry/compaction loss; end-to-end tests cover resumed runtime-cell reuse and compaction.
actions.description: Verify that every completion-bearing output has one preceding, type-correct exec or wait input with the expected origin and runtime handle, and make any loss of that evidence irreversible for the affected cell.

actions.intent: Keep each serialized tool result unambiguously correlated with the tool call that produced it.
actions.module_role: Conversation-history adapter at the structured tool-call boundary
actions.pre_state: Internal assistant tool calls and tool results contain matching identifiers, but serialization omits both identifiers because the capability predicate is false.
actions.post_state: For protocols classified as requiring IDs, each serialized function call and corresponding function response carries the same normalized identifier; protocols outside that class retain the prior omission behavior.
actions.validation: Serialize histories containing multiple calls and matching results, assert ordered ID equality on both sides for each supported adapter, and assert IDs remain absent for an older protocol version.
actions.description: Use the shared capability decision to serialize the same correlated identifier on both the function call and its response while retaining omission for protocols that do not require it.

actions.intent: Bound a loop whose tool arguments vary while its observable read-only operation remains unchanged.
actions.pre_state: No loop has fired, detection is enabled for the session, and incoming tool requests may repeatedly map to the same semantic inspection key.
actions.post_state: At the threshold the loop is marked detected with a dedicated reason and logged; before the threshold processing continues, while nonmatching calls, retries, and prompt resets clear the streak.
actions.validation: Verify no detection through threshold minus one, detection and telemetry at the threshold, streak restart after nonmatching calls and retries, and suppression after session disable.
actions.description: Track consecutive requests sharing the semantic inspection key, reset on progress or replay boundaries, and halt at the bounded threshold while respecting the explicit session override.

actions.intent: Keep unrelated complete tool-call inventories trustworthy when another output exceeds the metadata budget.
actions.pre_state: Serialized tool-call metadata exceeds argument, per-output, or request limits, so some evidence must be truncated or omitted.
actions.post_state: Optional result metadata and sources are shed first; an over-budget output carries its own omission marker; completion is cleared for every output sharing the damaged cell but remains available to intact unrelated cells.
actions.validation: Protocol tests exercise budget priority and fail-closed completion, recorder tests preserve an unrelated complete exec under overflow, and an end-to-end Code Mode test verifies the same behavior.
actions.description: Apply request-size limits per output, preserve stronger evidence before optional metadata, and revoke completion only where truncation or omission damaged the recorded inventory.

actions.intent: Keep metadata recording aligned with current runtime policy without altering which tools can execute or falsely certifying calls made before recording began.
actions.pre_state: A session's recording rollout may change after construction, or a legacy reload may carry the session's original feature snapshot rather than current host policy.
actions.post_state: Normal runtime refresh atomically creates or removes recorder state without changing execution gates; late-created state marks prior history unobserved, and legacy reload preserves the existing recorder.
actions.validation: Recorder and end-to-end tests verify runtime enablement, absence of completeness when earlier history was unobserved, and preservation of prepared call bindings across refresh.
actions.description: Allow runtime rollout configuration to enable or disable evidence recording independently from tool dispatch, while preventing stale legacy snapshots from replacing a valid live recorder.

actions.intent: Identify histories whose external structured-tool protocol requires explicit correlation identifiers.
actions.module_role: Protocol capability classifier shared by message serialization
actions.pre_state: The classifier recognizes existing model families but returns false for a newer protocol generation whose tool interactions require explicit IDs.
actions.post_state: The classifier returns true for the newer major-version boundary and existing required families, and false for the verified older version.
actions.validation: Evaluate representative identifiers immediately below and above the version boundary plus existing true cases; expect Gemini 2.5 false and Gemini 3.6, Claude, and GPT-OSS true.
parameters: minimum major version requiring explicit IDs
actions.description: Extend the shared capability predicate at the version boundary while preserving existing model-family behavior and excluding older versions.

actions.intent: Prevent identifier reuse or unavailable history from producing a false tool-call completion claim.
actions.pre_state: A recorder may encounter call origins or runtime handles that were already present in initial history, reused during the session, or unavailable because historical indexing exceeded a safety bound.
actions.post_state: Completion can begin only for identifiers proven fresh against bounded historical and live observations; collisions, oversized identifiers, and incomplete history indexing fail closed.
actions.validation: Bounded-filter tests verify namespace separation and saturation behavior; recorder tests verify that paginated known IDs and reused origins are rejected while genuinely fresh origins remain usable.
actions.description: Maintain bounded, monotonic knowledge of historical and live identifiers so reused or unindexable identifiers cannot be treated as fresh evidence for completion.

actions.intent: Recognize repeated operations that are semantically equivalent despite argument variation without misclassifying productive shell work.
actions.pre_state: A shell tool request contains an unclassified command string that may have multiple chained segments.
actions.post_state: The request has either one stable overview-inspection key or no stagnation key; write-bearing, mixed-purpose, non-repository, and path-specific review commands have no key.
actions.validation: Feed positive command variants and negative boundary cases through the always-on checker; only complete chains of overview-style read-only inspections may contribute to the common streak.
actions.description: Normalize syntactically varied shell requests into one stagnation class only when every command segment performs repository-wide read-only inspection, while treating productive or narrowly targeted commands as progress.

interpretation.action_reuse: An Action is reusable only when its semantic owner, finite operation, state transition, and validation oracle all survive substitution into the other repository.
interpretation.workflow_reuse: A repeated role sequence such as establish-contract -> reconcile -> validate is a reusable Workflow fragment, but it is a template over new Actions rather than evidence that the Actions themselves are interchangeable.
interpretation.granularity: A split is justified only when a candidate contains independently testable finite operations with separate postconditions or validation oracles. Different paths, providers, or filenames alone are not a reason to split.
